newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps slide lower, mogas falls another $2.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps slide lower, mogas falls another $2.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly weaker on Thursday morning with soft oil futures.
Gasoline sunk $2 a tonne, fuel was down $1 but Brent crude CFDs edged higher and crack spreads against Brent were well bid.
Gasoline fell another $2 a tonne for May swaps with offers at $193 by lunchtime and at $190.50 for June. Physical barges traded at $188.50 and $193 for loading 1-15 May.
Gasoline crack spreads against Brent were little changed with June at $4.95 a barrel and the third and fourth quarters were pegged around $4.10 and $3.10 respectively.
Gas oil against Brent remained well bid but levels were little changed from Tuesday at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Heavy fuel eased 50 cents a tonne to $81.50 for May and $87 for low sulphur. Dealers said the market remains depressed in Europe with only minimal demand from power companies and shipowners. But they also saw support from Asia where swaps edged up 41 a tonne to over $98 for May.
At least one cargo from the Mediterranean may head for Asia, dealers said.
Brent CFDs were broadly unchanged with next week slipping a few cents but the week after a similar amount higher.
Next week traded at 59 cents under June but then fell back to 61 cents under with the following week around 53 cents under.
Wet Brent was steady at about in what dealers said was a slow market for North Sea crudes.
